description: En Space Raccoons adoptamos el ingenio y la curiosidad de los mapaches para descifrar retos complejos de la NASA con soluciones prácticas e innovadoras. Combinamos habilidades en tecnología, diseño y resolución ágil de problemas en un entorno de trabajo colaborativo y competitivo, y buscamos integrantes con ganas de sumar en programación, análisis de datos, diseño o comunicación para completar el equipo.
summary: KetzaMed is an offline health monitor for astronauts on long space missions. It tracks sleep, stress, mood, heart rate, radiation and space weather for the whole crew, compares each value with the astronaut’s own baseline, and raises OK, WATCH or ALERT states with a clear explanation of why. It also includes SÝNERIS, an assistant that answers health questions, prepares reports for Earth and, as a dog or cat companion, offers emotional support against isolation. KetzaMed addresses the challenge of keeping crews healthy far from Earth by combining NASA-STD-3001 measurements, radiation and solar-event estimates, and early-warning trends in one tool built in Python. It matters because delayed communication and limited medical staff mean small changes must be noticed early, and because crew autonomy and mental health are key for future Moon and Mars missions.
details:
What it does and how it works
KetzaMed monitors the health of a whole crew on a local computer, with no internet needed. Astronauts log or import daily data (sleep, heart rate, HRV, SpO2, temperature, blood pressure, mood, stress, social contact, exercise, radiation, CO2 and ECG). Each measure is checked against an absolute limit, the astronaut’s own baseline, the 7-day trend and sudden changes, and is classified as OK, WATCH or ALERT. The software also shows history and trends, compares crew members, estimates radiation exposure and solar-event risk using public NOAA space weather data, and has an Earth Link text channel. The assistant SÝNERIS searches a medical knowledge base (BM25) and says when it is not sure. Emergency phrases always take priority.

Benefits
Early detection of small changes, clear explanations of every alert, crew autonomy during communication delays, health data kept on the local computer, and emotional support against isolation.

Expected impact
Help future Moon and Mars crews notice problems before they become serious, reduce dependence on Earth for routine health decisions, and support mental well-being during long confinement.

Tools, languages, hardware and software
Python 3.11+ (standard library: HTTP server, SQLite, Tkinter, unittest), HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the web interface, the browser Web Speech API for voice, optional Piper (local neural voice) and optional Ollama (local language model for non-medical chat), Playwright for testing and ffmpeg for the promo video. Hardware: a regular computer and a smartwatch for heart rate; Bluetooth sensor support is implemented but still needs tests with real devices. We also used Claude (Anthropic) as an AI development assistant.

What makes it creative
Instead of a cold dashboard, the assistant is a pet companion (dog or cat) with a natural voice and a 3D hologram whose mouth follows the audio. The astronaut can name it, talk to it, and use it as a journal. The interface colors are fully customizable.

Factors our team considered

  • Autonomy and privacy: everything runs offline and locally.
  • Safety: emergency phrases override casual chat, and health words never reach the optional language model.
  • Honesty: it is a support prototype, not a medical device, and the thresholds are illustrative and need validation by flight surgeons.
  • Accessibility: Spanish and English, readable color contrast and editable colors.
  • Trust: every value keeps its source, and hand-written values are never overwritten by imports.
